notes.key_messages: To succeed in this paper candidates need to have completed full syllabus coverage, remember necessary formulae, show all necessary working clearly and use a suitable level of accuracy.
notes.general_comments: The paper gave the opportunity for candidates to demonstrate their knowledge and application of mathematics. The majority of the candidates were able to use the allocated time to good effect and complete the paper. It was noted that the majority of candidates answered all of the questions with some omitting parts of a question on a particular topic. The standard of presentation and amount of working shown was generally good. In particular candidates showed improvement in their drawing of curves. Few instances of joining points with straight lines were evident. There were still a few instances of candidates rubbing out construction lines and/or working in questions, losing marks for themselves. Candidates should be encouraged to show clear working in the answer space provided; the formulae used, substitutions and calculations performed are of particular value if an incorrect answer is given. Candidates need to be aware of the correct way to convert answers from, for example, grams to kilograms.
notes.1a: This part was generally well answered with most of the candidates scoring full marks. Occasionally a candidate lost marks due to giving answers to two significant figures instead of three.
notes.1bi: Candidates understood that they had to add their five values and many correct answers were seen.
notes.1bii: Although candidates understood that they had to subtract their previous answer from 10, several lost the mark because they just gave an answer of 0.5 or 0.50 instead of 0.53.
notes.1ci: This was generally well answered. The most common error was to assume that there are 100 minutes in an hour.
notes.1cii: This was also generally well answered with the majority of candidates understanding the required ratio. However, a common error was to not express it in its simplest form with many leaving it as 18:45.
notes.1d: Many candidates gave the correct answer. Working would have been useful here as a number of candidates just gave the rounded answer of 35 with no working to show where it had come from.
notes.2ai: The range was generally well found. The most common error was to write 9 - 20 instead of 11. A few candidates wrote down 3 or 12 – 15 which appears to be an attempt at the range of the middle two numbers.
notes.2aii: Although a large majority of candidates gave the correct answer, many others calculated the median instead.
notes.2aiii: This part was not answered quite as well as the previous part. Common errors included finding the median without ordering the data or rounding the answer to a whole number.
notes.2aiv: Many candidates gave the correct answer. A common error was to miss out one of the terms when adding, or incorrectly adding. If candidates showed working they could gain part marks.
notes.2bi: The table was generally completed accurately.
notes.2bii: The majority of candidates understood how to interpret data as a pie chart. When a pie chart was drawn most of the candidates labelled the sectors correctly. In a few cases incorrect angles were drawn.
notes.2c: Although a clear majority of candidates scored full marks there was a sizeable minority who did not answer this part. A common error was to not give the answer in its lowest terms. Common incorrect answers seen were 3/12 and 3/5.
notes.3a: Most candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.3b: Again most candidates gave the correct answer. Half of those who did not, gave the distance from Bruce’s home at 09 20.
notes.3c: Candidates understood the need to divide the distance by the time. However, the majority of them did not carry out one or other of the necessary conversions in the distance (metres to kilometres) and/or in the time (minutes to hours).
notes.3d: Many candidates drew the correct graph. Those that did not draw the correct graph, the majority made a mistake in the line representing the journey from the park to Bruce’s home with many finishing at the end of the graph (10 15 instead of 10 10).
notes.4ai: Many candidates gave the correct answer. A few reflected the shape in the wrong line.
notes.4aii: Again many candidates gave the correct answer. Some candidates gave answers where they rotated clockwise about C and others rotated anticlockwise or clockwise about the reflection of C .
notes.4bi: Some candidates gave the full correct answer. A greater number made a mistake in the column vector, the common error being mistakes in the signs.
notes.4bii: Few candidates scored full marks with the vast majority only giving two of the three pieces of information needed to describe an enlargement. Common incorrect answers seen for the scale factor were 2 and − . − 9 ⎛ ⎞ 1 ⎜ ⎟
notes.5ai: Many candidates gave the correct answer. A common error was to find the interior rather than exterior angle.
notes.5aii: About half the candidates recognised that the lines were parallel. Of these a small majority could give the correct reason. There was a large number of candidates who gave an incorrect statement such as perpendicular or similar, or did not provide an answer.
notes.5b: The correct answer was often seen. Candidates could improve by recognising that a tangent and radius form a right angle.
notes.5c: Again the correct answer was often seen. A common incorrect answer was 9.
notes.6a: Many candidates completed the table correctly. The most common error was to give y=4 at x= -2.
notes.6ci: Most candidates understood the concept of line of symmetry.
notes.6cii: If a line had been drawn in the previous part the correct answer was often seen. The common incorrect answer seen was y=1.
notes.6d: Candidates understood how to use a graph to solve an equation. In some cases candidates attempted to use the quadratic formula when they had not drawn a graph. The most common error was to misread the scale.
notes.7a: Almost every candidate completed the table correctly.
notes.7c: Few candidates gave the correct answer. Some candidates lost marks because they did not show any working. The most common error was to calculate the mean shoe size ignoring the frequency giving an answer of 4.75.
notes.8bi: A small majority of candidates gave the correct construction. The most common error was to draw the angle bisector using a protractor.
notes.8bii: Candidates who had drawn an angle bisector measured a length although some were inaccurate.
notes.8ci: Nearly all candidates performed the same in this construction as in the previous one in part (b)(i) .
notes.8cii: Although many candidates measured the correct angle even more measured the acute angle instead of the obtuse angle or left the answer blank.
notes.8d: Some candidates did show that they understood how to find the region. This was the least successful part of the question with many just shading any part of the triangle, and on occasions, almost hiding answers to other parts of the question.
notes.9ai: Many correct answers were seen. The common incorrect answer seen was 1500.
notes.9aii: Candidates understood the necessary calculation and many gave the correct answer. The most common errors were to divide by the density and/or incorrectly converting from grams to kilograms.
notes.9bi: A good majority of candidates showed this by using Pythagoras’ theorem. Some candidates attempted to use trigonometry but tended to make mistakes and to make premature approximations.
notes.9bii: This part proved challenging for many candidates. The most common error was to not include all of the five surface areas. However, many successfully obtained the total cost for their surface area.
notes.10aii: Although some candidates gave the correct answer the majority gave pw as the answer, missing the fact that the total distance was required.
notes.10aiii: This part proved more challenging. Candidates understood that they needed to divide a distance by a time but did not recognise that the total time was required.
notes.10bi: Many candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.10bii: The correct answer was often seen. The most common error was to incorrectly re-arrange the formula. 1200 + pw
notes.11a: The vast majority of candidates gave the correct next term in all four sequences. th (b) Many candidates were not able to write down an expression for the n term in either sequence. th Candidates would benefit by understanding the ways in which n terms are generated.
notes.11ci: Many candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.11cii: Many candidates gave the correct answer. A common error was to substitute 592 for n instead of th making the n term equal to 592.
notes.11ciii: The correct answers were sometimes seen. Many candidates did not see the correct pattern of terms in the entire sequence but used a pattern from a few consecutive terms to give answers. 2 2
